title: fix(cli): serve's boot-quiet window buffers plugin log lines instead of discarding them (#4012)
body:
Closes #4012.

## The drain

`serve` blanks stdout while the kernel boots so the startup banner is readable. That window dropped what it intercepted:

```js
process.stdout.write = (chunk, ...rest) => {
  if (bootQuiet) return true;  // swallow
  ...
};
```

`ObjectLogger` routes `debug`/`info`/`warn` to **stdout** and only `error`/`fatal` to stderr — so that one line swallowed every boot-phase `logger.warn` any plugin emits. `os dev` spawns `serve` with inherited stdio, so a single drain blinded both entrypoints at every log level.

That also explains the issue's two puzzles. `--log-level debug` streamed 2,360 data-phase lines with zero boot-phase ones because the sink was live all along — just not until after the window closed. And the `⚠` lines that *did* appear reached the terminal via `console.warn`, which writes to stderr and was never patched — the same reason the `DEGRADED BOOT` datasource notices had already been worked around into bare `console.*`.

It inverted the flag's own promise, too: the default is `warn` precisely *"so flow/hook execution failures surface (ADR-0032)"*.

## The fix

The window is worth keeping, so it becomes a buffer rather than a drain — the issue's option (2).

- **`BootLogCapture`** (new, `packages/cli/src/utils/boot-log-capture.ts`) is a line-oriented, bounded sink for the intercepted bytes. It classifies each line against `ObjectLogger`'s three renderings (pretty / text / json, ANSI-stripped) and retains only records at `warn` or above, so buffer size tracks a boot's *warnings* rather than its chattiness. Chunks that split mid-line are carried across writes, and a trailing unterminated record still flushes — that is the shape the last warning before a crash arrives in.
- The retained records **replay under the banner**, beside the automation and seed summaries that already exist for exactly this reason. The startup chatter the window exists to hide is still dropped.
- **Three exits carry them, not just the healthy one:** the banner, `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT` (a deploy pipeline must not lose a degraded-boot warning), and serve's error path — a boot that died is when its warnings matter most, and it never reaches the banner.
- At **`--verbose` / `--log-level debug|info` the window no longer opens at all.** Buffering a stream the operator explicitly asked to watch would be the flag defeating itself.

Option (1) from the issue — attach the sink before `bootstrap()` — turned out not to map onto the code: there is no sink to move. `Kernel` takes `logger?: Partial<LoggerConfig>` and builds its own `ObjectLogger`, and the "sink" is serve's stdout patch. Making it level-aware is the same idea landed where the mechanism actually lives.

## Verification

On `examples/app-todo`, before → after:

| | lines | WARN lines | `[action-governance]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `os serve` (before) | 25 | **0** | **0** |
| `os serve` (after) | 33 | **5** | ✅ names all 8 unbound actions |
| `os dev` (after) | — | **5** | ✅ |

```
  ⚠ Boot diagnostics — 5 warnings logged during startup:
    …WARN [auth] no cache service registered — rate-limit counters use a per-process in-memory store…
    …WARN [AppPlugin] [protocol] package 'com.example.todo' declares no engines.protocol range…
    …WARN Driver already registered, skipping {"driverName":"com.objectstack.driver.sql"}
    …WARN [action-governance] declared script actions with NO handler — a button wired to nothing (ADR-0078)…
         {"count":8,"actions":["todo_task:clone_task","todo_task:complete_task", … ]}
    …WARN StorageServicePlugin: storage adapter swapped (LocalStorageAdapter → LocalStorageAdapter)…
    run with --log-level debug to watch the boot stream live
```

## Tests

- **13 unit cases** pin the classifier and the buffer, driving a **real `ObjectLogger`** through the **real interception** — so a change to its line format fails here rather than silently reopening the hole. They also pin the other half of the split: an `info`-level host still gets a clean banner.
- **2 end-to-end cases** boot a real stack through `bin/run-dev.js` and read its stdout, using the issue's recipe with a config-only positive control (a declared `script` action with no handler, which the ADR-0110 D5 inventory always warns about). One asserts `[action-governance]` on stdout at the default level; the other asserts boot traces stream at `--log-level debug`.

Both e2e cases were confirmed to **fail against the pre-fix command** and pass after. Full CLI suite: 84 files / 877 tests green; `eslint src` clean.

## What the newly-visible warnings turned up — all filed separately

Making these lines visible immediately paid for itself. None of the following are touched by this PR:

- **#4095 — config-booted apps lose their `onEnable` hook.** The `[action-governance]` line above is not cosmetic: `POST /api/v1/actions/todo_task/complete_task` returns `404 Action 'complete_task' on object 'todo_task' not found`, and `--log-level debug` shows `No runtime.onEnable function found {"appId":"com.example.todo"}`. The example is correctly authored; the handlers never register, so all eight of its buttons are dead over HTTP. This is the ADR-0110 D5 checklist catching a real one on its first observable boot.
- **#4085 — `os serve <config>` cannot boot without a prebuilt `dist/objectstack.json`**, dying with `Service 'manifest' is async - use await` (reproducible on `examples/app-todo` by moving its artifact aside). The e2e fixture here runs `os compile` first for that reason.
- **#4096 — `StorageServicePlugin` warns "adapter swapped (LocalStorageAdapter → LocalStorageAdapter) … files may be unreachable" on every clean boot**, where nothing changed.
- **#4097 — example apps declare no `engines.protocol` range**, so ADR-0087's compatibility check is skipped on the very templates users copy.
